newsitem.title: USA: Ford Q3 U.S. incentives rise.
newsitem.headline: Ford Q3 U.S. incentives rise.

text.p: Ford Motor Co spent an average of $1,100 on retail incentives in the United States in the third quarter, up from both $850 a year ago and $945 in the second quarter of 1996.
The company's average profit per vehicle in the U.S. in the third quarter was $1,300, compared to $750 a year ago. The profit-per-vehicle number includes results from Ford's Financial Services Group.
Ford announced a third quarter profit Wednesday of $686 million or $0.56 a fully diluted share, compared to $357 million or $0.27 a year ago.

Although Ford has been spending heavily to push the Taurus to the No. 1 U.S. car spot, its U.S. marketing costs as a percentage of revenue fell to 6.8 percent in the third quarter from 7.1 percent a year ago and 9.0 percent in the second period of 1996.
Third quarter revenues climbed to $34 billion from $31.4 billion. Worldwide vehicle unit sales in the third quarter were also up, increasing to 1,452,000 from 1,435,000.

But the automaker lost market share in both the U.S. and western Europe. Ford ended the quarter with 24.5 percent of the U.S. car and truck market. Ford had 24.8 percent in both the second quarter of 1996 and the third quarter of 1995.
Ford lost a full point of share in western Europe, falling to 11.8 percent from 12.8 percent in the year-ago quarter. Ford's share in the second quarter was 12.0 percent.
Ford's U.S. fleet sales were 19 percent of total sales, up from 18 percent in the third quarter of 1995, but down from 26 percent in the second quarter.

Cars and trucks sold with leases as a percentage of retail sales were 21 percent, down from 23 percent in the second quarter, and up from 19 percent a year ago. Those sales do not include leases to fleet buyers.
